title: Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Toggle on or off the option to see the distance that Internal tools, an internal lines or internal shapes are from edges of the 2D Pattern that it is within. ### Location 2D Display toolbar ▶ Information Display ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) Line Property Editor ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D information ▶ Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025) ※Note: * **This only works with measuring Internal Shapes & Internal Lines within a Pattern.** This will only show the mouse distance when you are using the internal Shape tools. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121976345) ### ### Operation #### **Toggle on/off the view options:** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D information ▶ Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025) 2D Display toolbar ▶ Information Display ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) →Activated 2D distance measurements will show or disappear in the 2D window. #### **Use with Internal Shape tools** 1. Turn on the Show 2D measurements view options (see Location). 2. go to the 2D pattern Window ▶ 2D toolbar ▶ Internal Shape ▶Select any of the Internal Shape Tools (Internal Polygon/Line , Internal Rectangle, Internal Ellipse. or Dart). 3. Place the cursor over a pattern piece. →You will see the purple dashed lines and numbers that indicate the Cursor's distance to the 4 sides of a square pattern piece. (see image below) ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438072884505) (Image above shows the internal rectangle tool selected and 4 sets of purple dashed lines with numbers that indicate the Cursor's distance to the 4 sides of a square pattern piece.) ※Note: If you have no internal shapes in the scene or are on the wrong tools it will appear empty or that it does not work. Make sure to work within a 2D pattern and it will show. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121976345) #### **Activate Internal Line or Shape's 2D Measurement Options.** 1. Turn on the Show 2D measurements view options (see Location). →All 2D distance measurements are deactivated by default. 2. Select an internal shape or Single internal shape/Line. 3. Go to the Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements **For Shapes** * * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ To Center * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the center of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ to OUTLINE * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down **For Internal Line / Segment points** * * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ To Center * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down ※Note: * You can also apply the Internal Line options to an internal Shape's internal lines or segment point. * Adding, cutting, making modifications to an internal segment line will remove the measurements options and you will need to apply them again. * Selecting multiple lines or shapes does applies the operation to each individual asset they are not treated as a group.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for toggling the display of 2D distance measurements for internal tools, lines, and shapes within a pattern in version 2025 of the software.

title: New Library Window (2025)
content: ### Objective Access and float the New Library for increased workspace in 3D and 2D windows while easily exploring varied assets, enjoying more intuitive interaction with CONNECT for seamless content access, and creating custom libraries to build and manage your personal assets. Linking CONNECT and Marvelous Designer into one place, you can more easily navigate default and store assets collectively. **※Note:** Starting from **Marvelous Designer 2025.2** , the Library(Legacy) window has been integrated into the **New Library** window and is no longer available. * The assets previously managed in the Legacy Library are safely stored in your local folder and can be relinked to the New Library for continued use. * The New Library can be docked in the Editor just like the Legacy Library. * The fabric assets (V1 zfabs) previously available in the Legacy Library can still be accessed from the Fabric tab in the New Library. ### Library 1. The New Library can be accessed using the Marvelous Designer Library Button on the top right of the screen. 2. Drag the Library window to move it, or press the ESC key to quickly close it. ### ### Revert to Previous Library 1. Revert to the Previous Library used in older versions (2024.2 and earlier) by clicking the "Revert to Previous Library " icon at the bottom left of the Library window. 2. Switch back to the New Library by clicking the "Switch to New Library " icon at the bottom of the existing Library window. ### Explore Assets 1. Click the category to explore assets. Assets are categorized into five groups: Garment, Avatar, Fabric, Trim, and Scene. Each category offers default assets by Marvelous Designer and community assets by CONNECT. 2. Double-click an asset or drag and drop it into Marvelous Designer to open it immediately. Community assets are available for free items only, and used items can be found in Purchase tab. 3. Click Show Preview button to preview the file on a larger thumbnail. ### Custom Library 1. Create your own custom library to build and manage your assets by clicking the + icon ▶ Create New Library button at the top. 2. Click Add Folder to add folders from your desktop. ※Note: Right-click on the Library tab you created and select Rename. Or simply double-click the tab and enter a new name. Transfer your previously favorited folders and continue using them seamlessly in the new library by clicking Create New Library at the top, then clicking Transfer Previous Favorites
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in navigating the New Library in Marvelous Designer 2025.2, showcasing its enhanced features for managing assets, integrating with CONNECT, and creating personalized libraries for a more efficient and intuitive design experience.

title: Sculpt (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Sculpt garments using various brush tools. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Sculpt Tool ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037146393) ### Operation 1. Select Sculpt tool from the 3D Toolbar. The Sculpt dialog window will appear. 2. Select any Brush from the Brush toolbar. Check the brush Size and Focal settings when hovering over a 3D garment. 3. Adjust each attributes for each brush: Size, Focal, Realistic, Layer, Spacing, Depth 4. Click and drag on 3D garment to sculpt. Press Shift key on the keyboard while using any type of Brush tool to smooth out. 5. In Sculpt mode, the garment appears in gray by default. To change the garment's color during sculpting, enable the Custom Material option. When Custom Material is disabled, you'll see the garment's original texture. ### Brush Types ![Sculpt Wrinkle On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438051249433) | Wrinkle | Left-click and drag to create wrinkles on the brush area. (ver. 10) ---|---|--- ![Sculpt Release On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438116304537) | Release | Left-Click + Shift and drag to release wrinkles on brush area (ver. 10) ![Sculpt Sculpt On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037707161) | Sculpt | Emboss mesh. With invert option activated. engraves mesh. ![Sculpt Smooth On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037856025) | Smooth | Makes the surface flat on average. (Shortcut: Shift) ![Sculpt Grab On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438100099097) | Grab | Moves vertices to express pulled surface. ![Sculpt Stamp O_n.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438038186649) | Stamp | Use an image as a stamp. ![Sculpt Pinch On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438052527513) | Pinch | Close the position of the vertices, makes the surface sharper. ### Brush Property Depending on the type of brush, the properties you apply vary. Brush Property | Description | Brush Type ---|---|--- Wrinkle | Release | Sculpt | smooth | Grab | Stamp | Pinch Strength | Strength of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | O | O Size | Size of brush. | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Focal | Coverage of brush. (similar with Hardness) | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Spacing | Interval of brush. | X | X | O | X | X | X | X Depth | Depth of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | X | O Alpha | Using an image as brush. | X | X | O | X | O | O | X Invert | Change the direction of a brush. (shortcut: Alt) | X | X | O | X | O | O | X Realistic | Realistic (ver. 10) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X Layer | Layer (ver. 10) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X ### Option Custom Material | Allows assignment of a temporary material while the Sculpt Tool is activate. To maintain the Garment Rendering Style(e.g., monochrome, wireframe) from the 3D Window, disable this option. ---|--- Color | Specifies the color of the material. Roughness | Slider Adjusts surface roughness to control light diffusion. Metalness | Modifies reflection intensity to enhance the visibility of surface Curvature. Double Sides | Toggle on/off with Double Side option activated, apply custom material to both back and front side of mesh. #### **Using an Alpha Texture as Brush** 1. Click button next to Image. 2. Click an Image from default images. \- Focal setting is not available for image brush. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. To turn off an image, click button and select Off. \- Focal setting appears on brush property after turning off image. #### **Adding Alpha Texture** 1. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438038474137) button next to image. 2. Select an image on the file browser. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. After adding image, can load the image by clicking button next to the image. #### **Show/Hide 3D Pattern (Shortcut Shift + Q)** 1. Show selected pattern only \- Select a pattern while input Shift + Q, other patterns will be hidden. 2. Reverse selected pattern/hidden pattern \- After operating no.1 above, click on the selected pattern while input Shift + Q to reverse hidden pattern/ selected pattern. 3. Adding hidden patterns \- To hide additional patterns, click on a pattern which you want to hide while input Shift + Q. 4. Show All 3D Patterns \- Click on the background while input Shift + C (Shift + Q for Ver. 2024.2 and below) to show all pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Sculpt Tool in the 3D Window to enhance garment designs through various brush techniques and settings.

title: Schematic Render (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective View 3D Garments with outlines and details shown in a format similar to that of flat fashion sketches or stylized 2D sketches. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Render ▶ Schematic Render 3D Window ▶3D Display Render Options ▶ Schematic Render ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location above. → Render the 3D garment according to the schematic format. 2. Set the following options as needed. Option | **Description** ---|--- **Line Thickness** | Show or hide the silhouette line (the outline of the area where the garment and the background meet and the line of the wrinkled area inside the garment), Seamline, Internal Line and Topstitch line and adjust the line thickness. **Topstitch** | **(ver 2025.1)** Set specifications of Topstitches to achieve a visual appearance in the Schematic Render. 1. Click the Topstitch in Topstitch tab of the Object Browser. 2. In the Property Editor, activate the **Local Schematic Scale** option by clicking the checkbox. 3. Set the Topstitch parameters that appear below. * **Length** : Adjusts the length of each thread. * **Spacing** : Defines the spacing between each thread. * **Offset** : Adjusts the distance of the stitch from the edge of the applied line. * **Thickness** : Controls the visual thickness of the stitch thread. * **Width** : Sets the width of the stitch(especially Class 500 & 600 stitches). * **Distance** : Defines the distance between each stitch line. **Line Color** | Adjust the Color of the line. **Garment** | **Color** | Adjust the Color of the garment. **Texture** | The applied texture can be viewed as is. **Brightness** | Adjust the Brightness of the garment.
content_description: Explore and customize 3D garments with detailed outlines and schematic options to create visually striking representations similar to flat fashion sketches.

title: Edit Texture
content: ### Objective Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ Edit Texture 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Texture ### Operation **Move** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Click ▶ Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. **Zoom In/Out** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to zoom in/out. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Click ▶ Drag the diagonal line. 4. Enlarge or reduce the size of the selected texture image. → The selected texture image is now being adjustable while maintaining its horizontal and vertical ratios. 5. Click ▶ Drag the horizontal line in order to enlarge/reduce the texture image to up/down and left/right. → All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable corresponding to the axis direction. 6. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the image's Width and Height value in Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture Transformation. → The width and height of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjusted. **Rotate** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. 4. Drag around the circumference of the circle. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being rotated. **Rotate Grainline** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Click on a Pattern to rotate its grainline. → The selected Pattern's grainline is now being in black color. 3. Drag around the activated grainline, when the mouse cursor becomes in a shape of circular rotation. → The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. 4. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the angle value for grainline in Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ Grain Direction. → The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. 5. Simulate once it is adjusted. → The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. **Align Grain Parallel to Selected** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate its grain. → The grain of the selected Pattern is activated. → When multiple Patterns are selected, only the last Pattern's grain is activated, but the configuration is applied to all Patterns. 3. Right click on the Pattern and select Align Grain Parallel to Selected. →All selectable segments are highlighted. 4. Hover the mouse over the segment which the grain is to be aligned with. → The segment is highlighted in light blue. → The grain rotates. → When the selected segment is a curve, the grain rotates based on a line connecting the ends of the curve. 5. Click the desired segment. → The grain rotates parallel to the selected line. → When multiple Patterns are selected, all their grains rotate accordingly. **※ Note:** After selecting a Fabric, navigate to Property Editor ▶ Material ▶Transformation ▶Texture to type in the texture's width, height, and angle. Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. Edit back of texture when you change Garment Rendering Style as Back Texture Surface (ver. MD10)
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for modifying the grainline and positioning of individual patterns, as well as adjusting the rotation and size of texture images for specific fabrics within a design interface.

title: Auto Sewing (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Patterns are automatically sewn based on their placement on default avatars. ※Note: The available range of automatic sewing is as follows, * Top (T-shirts, Jackets, Jumpers, etc.)**** * Pants * Skirts ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Auto Sewing 3D Toolbar ▶ Auto Sewing ### Operation 1\. Click the Arrangement Points of the Avatar to arrange the Pattern. * Since Auto Sewing is calculated based on the information provided from the Arrangement Points make sure to place patterns on the correct arrangement points. **※ Note:** correct Arrangement Points should be used based on the rules below. Otherwise, Auto Sewing may not work properly. Collar/ Band | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's neck. ---|--- Bodies | Use Arrangement Points on the Avatar's body. Sleeves | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's arm, the cuffs can be used either arm/wrist Arrangement Points. Bottom | Use Arrangement Points at the legs. ※Note: Be mindful of arranging the pieces to auto-sew correctly. \- If the belt length includes a placket that is placed over the zipper, arrange the placket piece. \- Trace the internal line of the side pocket along the side seams. \- If the pants' width is large, arrange front and back pattern pieces separately by using each of the arrangement points. 2\. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. * Choose Garment type. (Top, Pants, Skirt) * For Tops: choose Front type from "Openable, Partially Openable, or Closed" * For Tops with "Closed" selected: choose "Collar seam". (Auto, Center Front, or Back Left) * Click OK. * The arranged patterns are automatically sewn. **※ Note:** * This feature will only work with the Default Bounding Volumes provided by Marvelous Designer, custom Bounding volumes & arrangement points will not work. * If sewing has been applied prior to automatic sewing, it is maintained while the rest of the sewing lines are being additionally auto-sewn. * Darts and Pleats can be sewn automatically without arranging patterns. * For Pleats, automatic sewing is possible only when Internal Lines are defined by the fold direction of the Pleats. * (Make sure your sewing line has segment points dividing the line for this operation to function properly)
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to guide users through the automatic sewing process for patterns on default avatars, ensuring accurate placement and operation for effective garment creation.

title: Rehost Software License Key to another environment
content: In order to move your software license key from one environment to another, please follow the steps below. * Please note that this rehost feature is only available if your software license key was generated as a “rehostable” type. ** If your Software License Key name includes “Rehostable” on the ACC page, you’re eligible to move a software license key to another environment. ([ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/devices.html)) **Step 1. Collect and Save Information - on a recipient device or PC** 1\. Open RUS on the destination machine that you want to transfer the SL license to ([**download**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vyPJ_ueKSbWWBUxKhZwM5K-hpmlHp4-l/view?usp=drive_link) the RUS) 2\. Click the ‘Transfer License’ tab on the top menu and click the box next to ‘Save recipient information to’. Then name the file according to your preference. 3\. Click ‘Collect and Save Information’, then the .id file will be saved on the destination machine. ![rus.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438428083865) **Step 2. Generate License Transfer File - on the original device or PC where the software license key is currently installed** 1\. Copy the .id file that was created from step 1 to the original machine which currently has the SL License installed. 2\. Open RUS and click the “Transfer License” tab. 3\. Find the software license key that you want to transfer under the ‘Key Type’ section and click. 4\. Load the .id file to ‘Read the recipient information file’ 5\. Click ‘Generate the license transfer file’ then name the file according to your preference. 6\. Click ‘Generate License Transfer File’ to create a .h2h file. ![rus1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438428256665) ![rus2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438433915545) **Step 3. After generating the file, the license will disappear from the source machine. As a result, the software license key is no longer installed on the original environment.** ![rus3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434055193) **Step 4. Apply Update** 1\. Once the .h2h file is created, copy the .h2h file to the destination machine. 2\. Open RUS again and click ‘Apply License File’ to load the file. 3\. Click ‘Apply Update’ ![rus4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434200601) **Step 5. You can now check the transferred License on your destination machine on the ACC page****( Link to **[**ACC Page**](http://localhost:1947/_int_/devices.html)**)** ![rus5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434332569)
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for transferring your rehostable software license key from one environment to another.

title: UV EDITOR MODE: UV Snapshot
content: ### Objective Saving UV as an image. (Ver. MD 7.5 +) ### Location Window ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV Snapshot Icon (Ver. 2025.0) Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV Snapshot Icon (2025.0) UV Editor mode Snapshot button on the toolbar at the top of the window. (up to Ver. 2024.2) ### Operation 1. Click the menu according to**Location.** 2. Click on the UV Snapshot icon. The Snapshot setting window will be opened. 3. Set the values for the following options below. Saving Path | Click the '...' folder icon button and set the saving directory and file format. Supports PNG and JPEG file formats. The background is not saved when saving PNG. When saving a JPEG, the background is saved as black. ---|--- Size (pixels) | Set the size of the image to be saved. The images are saved in a square with the same horizontal and vertical size. Antialiasing. If checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segments. Anti-alias Lines (Ver. 2025.0) | When the Anti-alias Lines option is checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segment. Wire Color | Sets the wire segment color. The color you set is not previewed in the UV correction window, and the corresponding color is applied when you save. UV Area | 0-1 (Default) | Save Default 0-1 Tile. A tile is a rectangular area between a single unit to a single unit. Selected Tile | Save a Selected Tile. If you enter the coordinates of U and V to be saved, one tile is saved accordingly. All Tiles | Save all Tile in which the UV appears 4. After setting values, click the save button to save the settings. The Snapshot image will be saved to the designated directory.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving UV snapshots as images in various formats using the UV Editor, detailing options for customization and file management.

title: Register Accessory: Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat .zacs (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Register the Avatar's Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat as an accessory file (ZACS). ### Location Main menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Register Accessory ### Operation #### **OBJ production** When making OBJ accessories in other 3D programs (Maya, 3ds Max, etc.), please follow the requirements below. * Set the work environment of the 3D program. (Axis: Y-Up, Unit: Millimeter) * Create a Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat OBJ according to the avatar file: Avatar | Prepare an avatar suitable for the Hair/Shoes to be registered. title: Create Smooth Curve
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Modify Pattern outlines or Internal Lines into smooth curves. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve 2. Click on a segment or point to establish the first point. → The point appears in grey. 3. Drag the mouse. → A grey arrow extending from the point follows the cursor. 4. Click on another segment or point to establish the endpoint. → A reference line is created between the two points. 5. With the reference line created, click on the side that will be converted into a smooth curve. → The entire side is highlighted in yellow. 6. Click & drag the reference line to create the desired smooth curve. → The entire outline of the selected side is replaced by the reference line. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438534208793) ### Updated in 2025.0 Curvature of a specific line can be precisely adjusted without affecting other lines. 1. Click a start point and endpoint on the segment or point to set the editing range. 2. Select which side to be edited. 3. Click and drag a segment or point to adjust curvature within the set range. * **Edit** * By default, nearby points adjust proportionally when moving. * You can move only the selected point by holding the [ D ] key while dragging. * Right-click while dragging the segment or point to enter a specific moving distance. * **Add** * Click a segment while holding the [ Ctrl ] key to add a curve point. _* Adding to a Bezier curve points convert it to free curve points, which may adjust the curvature._ * **Delete** * Right-click a point and click the Delete menu to delete selected points. 4. Press Enter to complete. * When selecting a pattern outline or internal line, update based on the edited pattern outline or internal line. * When selecting a reference line, update based on the edited reference line. Segment points will be added at the start and end. * ※ Note: #### Cancel Actions * Cancel All Actions: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Esc or Ctrl + Z on the keyboard and all actions are undone. * Cancel Last Action: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Delete or Backspace on the keyboard and the last action is undone.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Smooth Curve tool to transform pattern outlines or internal lines into smooth curves in a 2D design environment.

content: ### Objective Change the range, unit, and appearance of Garment Fit Maps. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Garment Fit Properties ### Operation [**[PDF] Workflow guide**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358145161113) 1. Check the following before using Garment Fitting Maps: * Fabric: Apply the fabric type that is appropriate for the design. * Avatar: Use an avatar in the right size. Adjust an avatar size according to your measurement chart or fitting model in the Avatar Editor. Main Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Avatar Size * Pose: Choose an avatar’s pose according to your style. Library > Avatar > choose the correct avatar version > Pose * Simulation: Change the Simulation Mode to Fitting (Accurate Fabric) or Animation (Stable) * Simulate every time after you change a design / fabric. 2. Open the Garment Fit Properties window from the Location above and modify its properties: **Fit Properties:** Properties | Description ---|--- Stress | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | kPa | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in kPa of the fabric that causes garment deformation. gf/cm2 | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in gf/cm2 of the fabric that causes garment deformation. mmHg | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in mmHg of the fabric that causes garment deformation. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. Face | The color map will be applied on the face of the garment. Point | The color map will be applied on the points of the mesh. Show | Select or deselect Weft / Warp / Shear to be included in the fit properties. Strain | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | % (percent) | The strain map is calculated through percentage. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. Face | The color map will be applied on the face of the garment. Point | The color map will be applied on the points of the mesh. Show | Select or deselect Weft / Warp / Shear to be included in the fit properties. Pressure | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | kPa | Displays the force per unit area in kPa applied to a garment by external stress. Represents the internal stress and tension in the fabric itself when stretched. gf/cm2 | Displays the force per unit area in gf/cm2 applied to a garment by external stress. Measures the actual pressure exerted by the garment on the body surface. mmHg | Displays the force per unit area in mmHg applied to a garment by external stress. Measures the compression pressure applied by the garment to the body. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. title: [Beta] Fur Rendering in 3D Window (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Express fur more realistically by adjusting Fur Parameters and Fur Shape to visualize different shaped and color fur in the 3D window. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Type ▶ Fur_Strand ### Operation 1. Apply the Fur_Strand material from the material type option, referring to the **'Location'** indicated above. * Fur can be previewed in 3D Window with Default Render and Quality Render, and Interactive Render. 2. Select one of the presets to express Fox, Mink, Angora, Sherpa and more. **Fur Material Properties** **Properties** | **Description****** ---|--- Texture Mapping | Repeat | Controls how many times the texture pattern repeats across the fur surface. Higher values create more repetitions of the pattern, resulting in a denser appearance. Unified | When enabled, applies the texture consistently across all fur strands for a uniform look. When disabled, each strand uses the texture based on its individual position, creating more natural variation. Type | Select Fur_Strand to edit Fur Parameters and Fur Shape. Fur Preset | Select Fur preset from Default, Angora, Fox, Mink Skin, Mohair, Muskrat Belly, Plush, Rabbit, Raw Edge Denim, Terry Cloth and Custom. Materials | Set the [Fabric properties](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425). Fur Parameters | Melanin | Configure the saturation of the fur's original color. Higher Melanin values create more saturated colors, while lower values result in lighter colors. Pheomelanin | Configure how reddish the fur appears. Higher Pheomelanin values create redder fur. The Pheomelanin value is applied proportionally to the Melanin value and has no effect when Melanin is set to 0. Glossiness | Configure the shininess of the fur. Higher values make the fur appear shinier when light is applied. Softness | Adjust the smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness values create smoother fur, while lower values result in rougher fur. Fur Gradation Color | Color | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. Position | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. Interpolation | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. Fur Shape | Base | Length (mm) | Configure the length of the fur. Higher the value is, longer the fur is. Thickness (mm) | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. Higher the value is, thicker the fur is. Bend | Configure the bending strength of the fur. Higher the value is, more affected by the gravity and bends more. Taper | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. Higher the value is, thinner the fur becomes toward the end. On the other hand, lower the value is, similar the thickness is between the root and the end. Density (inch2) | Configure how fur are closely placed. Higher the value is, more dense the fur is. On the other hand, lower the value is, more scattered the fur is. Segments | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has higher Bending value, the fur must have higher Segments value to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for the short and straight fur, the Segments value is not as significant. Maps | Use Base Maps to express different length, thickness, density, curl, gravity, bend, bend direction and initial direction within a single Pattern. 0 is multiplied to the values when a Map is black. On the other hand, 1 is multiplied to the values when a Map is white. ![renderoutput.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438303075481) Gravity | Force | Apply the force of gravity. Vector | Manually apply the Gravity value to each axis. Curl | Radius (mm) | Configure the size of the curl. Higher values create larger curls, while lower values create smaller curls. Number | Configure the number of curls. Higher values create more curls in the fur, while lower values create fewer curls. Variance | Length | Express uniform or irregular fur length. Higher values create more irregular fur lengths, while lower values create more uniform lengths. Thickness | Express uniform or irregular fur thickness. Higher values create more irregular fur thickness, while lower values create more uniform thickness. Direction | Express uniform or irregular fur bending direction. Higher values create more irregular bending directions, while lower values create more uniform bending directions. Gravity | Express uniform or irregular gravity effect. Higher values create more irregular gravity effects, while lower values create more uniform gravity effects. ※Note: Gravity effect only applies when the Bending value is not 0. Curl Radius | Express uniform or irregular curl radius. Higher values create more irregular curl radius, while lower values create more uniform curl radius. Randomization | Seed | Change the seed value to generate a different random pattern for the fur. Each seed creates a unique but consistent variation. 3. Select a fur preset from Physical Properties and fine-tune the physical property details to meet your specific requirements. ※Note: * Fur Strand is supported only in the window system at this moment. * Fur Strand is not currently supported for macOS due to rendering speed considerations. * Fur_Strand can be applied to all objects except Avatar and Stitch. * If you create Fur_Strand and export USD, there would be an option to include fur strand data.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to adjusting fur parameters and shapes in 3D modeling, allowing users to visualize and customize various fur types and colors for realistic rendering.

title: Avatar Editor (ver. 2025.0)
content: Avatar Settings Avatar Size Measure Arrangement Fitting Suit IK Joint ### ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Avatar Settings ### Objective Adjust the Avatar settings, such as size, measurement, arrangement, fitting suit, and IK settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ### Operation 1. Place an Avatar in the 3D window. The Avatar Editor is accessible only when the avatar is in the 3D window. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated above under Location. → Avatar Editor window will appear. 3. Adjust the properties for the properties below. There are separate tabs for Avatar Size, Measure, Arrangement, Fitting Suit, and IK Joint. ### # Avatar Size Avatar size allows you to create a custom-size avatar with your own measurements. The Marvelous Designer Avatar Editor is powered by real body scan data to help you create realistic body shapes, whether you have a complete size specification or not. ### #### **Size:** Option | Description ---|--- Size | Custom / Presets | Select an Avatar size from the presets, or create an avatar with your desired size by inputting detailed measurements. From the dropdown, presets include standard sizing such as Curvy, Straight, Petite Curvy, Petite Straight, Plus Curvy and Plus Straight for women, and size 34 to 52 Standard for men. Additional size measurements can be added and entered in the "Set Details" from the gear icon. Avatar Name (.avs) | Select the Avatar file. Units of measurement | Select from Millimeter, Centimeter, Inch, Feet & Inch. Set Details (gear icon) | By clicking this icon, you can select and activate currently hidden size measurements. When checked on, they will become available in the Size section for editing. Show all Measurements (list icon) | By clicking this icon, you can view active and hidden size measurements that are not displayed in the editor window. If the measure is not checked on in the Set Details it will be visible, but not editable. Width / Height | The Width/Height categories allow you to select what you want the key measures to be for your size, and Marvelous Designer will then automatically generate a proportionate body shape based on these key measures. For example, if Under Bust and Total Height are selected here, circumference, height, and length measures below will be automatically created or slightly adjusted to maintain a proportional body shape. Link (default) | Size editing for Marvelous Designer avatars is algorithm-based, and by default, measures are linked to help you create a proportional body shape based on real human body scan data. Unlink | You can unlink the proportional editing by clicking the icon to deactivate it. When unlinked, any changes to the key Width/Height measurements will not affect the lower measurements. #### **Shape:** Option | Female | Male | Kid | Baby ---|---|---|---|--- Shape | Hand & Head | Hand | O | O | X | X Head | O | O | O | X Crotch | Width | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Hip | Dips | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Breast | Shape | O | X | X | X Space | O | X | X | X Height | O | X | X | X ### **Custom Avatar Size (recommended workflow)** 1. Go to Avatar > Avatar Editor to open the editor. Load the Avatar *.AVT and ensure it is the version you want to apply your size to. 2. If you are editing from an existing *.AVS file, click the open icon to select your file. When open, the avatar measures will be displayed in the 3D window. Measures that can be moved will appear as black dotted lines, and non-editable measures will be grey dotted lines. 3. Before entering size data in the editor window, ensure the desired values are available. If not, click the Set Details button to add them and Exit to go back to the main editor. For optimal results, it is recommended to activate only the measurements that you have. 4. Once you have your avatar and desired measures, select your key measures for Width / Height and enter your values. It is recommended to keep the default Link option on, but if desired, click the icon to unlink. 5. Now enter your desired measurements in circumference, height, and length. Note that when linked, Marvelous Designer will make slight automatic adjustments to maintain a proportional body shape. ※Note: When developing categories such as gloves, intimates, and headwear, you have additional options to adjust the head, hands, crotch, and bust to suit your needs. 6. Press Save to save your custom Avatar. After creating a custom size, you have the option to save the size only (*.AVS) or as an Avatar (*.AVT). The steps to modify the measurements of an Avatar are the same whether saving an *.AVT or an *.AVS file. The only difference is the way you open the file. #### **File Format** File name | Description ---|--- Avatar (.AVT) | The *.AVT is a Marvelous Designer native format, which contains all the information related to Avatars, including the model, skeleton rig, sizing, pose, motion, accessories, bounding volumes, and arrangement points. Avatar Size (.AVS) | The *.AVS format contains avatar size information. The Avatar file must be loaded before opening an *.AVS size file. The *.AVS format does not contain any avatar, only size information. ※Note: It is not possible to mix *.AVS files between avatars of different versions, age, or gender. The *.AVS file is only compatible with the avatar on which it was originally created. For example, if you created an *.AVS file using a female V2 Avatar, this will only apply to the female V2 Avatar. Saving in .AVS You can connect the folder you saved to your library and click-drag your different sizes on the avatar of your project file. You can open an .AVS file, using the Folder Icon next to Save in the Avatar Editor. Saving in .AVT If you want to add a custom Avatar in the workspace, open from File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Measure You can use 6 types of avatar tape that allow you to create free measures, circumference, linear, and height measurements. Please see the [**Measure manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358154578585-Avatar-Measure-above-ver-10) for additional Measure information. All added measurements can be viewed and renamed in the Measure tab. ※Note: The difference between ‘Basic’ and ‘Surface’ is whether the measure will follow the curvature of the avatar's body or follow a direct line around the widest points. The Basic Tapes are most akin to methods of measuring the body with soft measuring tape, whereas ‘Surface’ will measure along the curved surface of the body. #### **Measure:** Option | Description ---|--- Measure | Name | The default name appears after creating a new measure. Double-click on the text to rename. Delete | Delete the selected Measure. ※Note: You can also use the Edit Measurement tool to select the Tape Measure in the 3D Window and hit either the Backspace or Delete key. Fit to Avatar | Re-fit the measurements when changing its Pose or loading another Avatar's joints. Open | Open a *.MEA file created with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. Save | Save the measurements in *.MEA format to open with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. ※Note:.MEA files should be applied to the same model in the same version. Measurement Type | Toggle the Measurement Type between Basic and Surface to update the type without needing to recreate the measurement. Measurement Information | Measurement Information given is either Tape or Circumference. Basic Length | Check the value when measured with the Basic Measurement tool. Surface Length | Check the value when measured with the Surface Measurement tool. Show | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. Show Length | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Arrangement Edit, add or delete any of the Bounding Volumes or Arrangement Points in the Arrangement tab. Please see the [Arrangement manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/47114831810969) for additional information on how to use Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points. You can rename any Bounding Volume and Arrangement Point with "NAME_1_L", "NAME_1_R" to maintain symmetry. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default. #### **Bounding Volume:** Option | Description ---|--- Board | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new Bounding Volume called “PAN” will be added at the bottom of the list. Delete | Deleted the selected Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes | Reset to the original position Open | Open a pre-saved *.PAN file Save | Save the created *.PAN file to use with other avatars. Joint Name 0 | Set the beginning location of the Joint (X-ray) Joint Name 1 | Set the end location of the Joint (Show Avatar Joint) Height | Set the height Radius X (mm) | Set the horizontal radius Radius Y (mm) | Set the vertical radius Hands/Feet | Toggle on to extend BV's length to Avatar's hands or feet, respectively #### **Point:** Option | Description ---|--- Placement | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new arrangement point named “Arrangement Point” will be created at the bottom of the list. Note that the point is unassigned by default, and you will need to select the BV and X Y positions in the steps below. Delete | Delete the selected Arrangement Point. Open | Open an *.ARR file; this can be used to apply Arrangement points to an *.OBJ avatar. Save | Save as an *.ARR file and open on another Avatar. Note: Some readjustment may be needed when applying to another avatar. Arrangement BV | Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point is to be placed. X | Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y | Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset | Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction | Wrapping can be set to up or down and will determine the direction of the pattern wrap when placed on the Arrangement Point. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Fitting Suit 1. Draw lines on the avatar according to the indicated position below. 2. Create the circumference line on the avatar's position following the image. • The pattern of the fitting suit is displayed. • The circumference line on both sides is automatically created symmetrically. 3. After creating all the circumference lines, click the Drape Fitting Suit button. • The fitting suit is draped. Adjust the fitting in the 3D window if needed. Option | Description ---|--- Fitting Suit | Auto Create Fitting Suit | Click this icon to create a fitting suit automatically. If the avatar is not created properly, we recommend creating it manually. Create Symmetric Tape | Toggle on and off to create the draw line symmetric or not symmetric. Delete | Delete the drawing line. Reset | All drawing lines will be deleted. Save | Save as an *.AVT file. **![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) ** # IK Joint Use IK joint mapping with various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ※ Note: The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. Operation | Description ---|--- Open / Save | You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. Click Open / Save icon at the top right to open or save IK data as a .iks file. ※Note: IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped. Auto Mapping | If the avatar meets the following conditions, click Auto Mapping at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the Marvelous Designer avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman. Set T-Pose | Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with Marvelous Designer avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped. Click Set T-Pose button. Reset Pose | If T-Pose is set correctly, this button activates, allowing you to check the Set T-pose when clicked. After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click this button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. ****
content_description: The Avatar Settings page allows users to customize and adjust avatar properties including size, measurements, fitting suits, and IK joint settings for optimal character design in 3D modeling.

title: Enterprise License Management Guide
content: Enterprise accounts are divided into Company ID and End User ID. For Enterprise Accounts, End User IDs (used to access software) are managed by Company IDs. To get better understanding on characteristic of each account and structure, please refer to the link below. * [Account Manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358380019737) **How Can I Manage My Licenses?** To manage your licenses, you will first need to login with your Company ID, at a page below. * [Account Login Page](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/member/signin) On “License Account Admin” you can view all licenses you’ve had in the past, upcoming expiration dates, delete/add end users, purchases licenses, view active end users, etc. You can access License Account Admin upon after the login, by clicking on your profile icon. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438023097369)![image \(5\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437990997657) _(sample image)_ On your “Dashboard”, you can view weekly average access to licenses, how many times licenses were used, how long do users spend on the software on average and etc. _*Denied access_ Denied Access refers to concurrent access being exceeded by users. For example, if you have 10 licenses, your concurrent access will be for 10 seats. If you are sharing the 10 licenses among 20 people, this feature lets you know that one of the 10 individuals will have to log out if another user needs access, or it may be time for you to purchase additional seats. The data is only valid for the network (floating type) license holders. The contact information is also provided on the left bottom of the screen for regional managers. Regional managers can help you with how to use the License Management services, and answer any questions. Based on the location you have set for your account, you will have different regional managers. If the listed regional managers are out of office, please feel free to contact md.bizdev@marvelousdesigner.com to reach out to the entire business development team. **How Do I Know What Licenses I Have and What Can I Do With Them?** Click on the “License” tab on your left menu which will bring you to this page. ![image \(6\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437977588249) _(sample image)_ **Filter section** In this section, you can search End User IDs or an email address to quickly look for the End User ID you are looking for, set to view active and expired licenses, perpetual/monthly/yearly/trial licenses and different versions of licenses. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437977795481) _(sample image)_ **License detail section** In this section, you can see every End User ID under your Company ID. You can view information such as the email address attached to the End User ID, plan type, license type, license count, current software version, and expiration dates. You can also directly add/extend your existing seats, or purchase a new license through this menu option. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438040393497) _(sample image)_ **Add/extend option** You can add another license to the same End User ID or extend the license period before the period ends. Both actions can only be done before the license expires. **New license option** New License option allows you to renew licenses past the expiration date. This action can only be done after the license expires. **Trade-In option** Perpetual license is eligible for our 'Trade-In' service, which is to convert perpetual license to annual type. Please refer the link below for more detailed information on this. * [Trade-In Policy](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/support/news?postId=233762c17aa04616bb0367f0f9561371) **License ID (End User) detail section** Clicking the individual license ID (End User) from the previous image on the left hand side, will lead you to the single End User detail page. In this page, you can manage End User IDs by viewing the user details, your password for the End User, the email address and the IP address when the license is being used at corporate premises. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438008453657) _(sample image)_ **What Else Can I Expect from License Account Admin page?** **User Pool** Within User Pool feature we provide, licenses are now much flexible in terms of management. Please read a separate manual followed by the link below, for better understanding of the usability around this feature. * [**User Pool Manual**](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358149827609) **Invoice** In the invoice section, you can view your past orders and invoices. You can also add and edit your billing address within this section.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing Enterprise accounts, detailing the structure of Company IDs and End User IDs, along with the tools and resources available for license management.

title: Marvelous Designer to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content: This guide outlines the workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. Step 1. Import USD Asset Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman Step 3. Create Cloth Asset Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset Step 5. Organize Assets Step 6. Create Outfit Asset Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility * * * ## Step 1. Import USD Asset ## ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018460697) 1. In the **Content Drawer** , import your Clothing USD Asset created in Marvelous Designer into the desired folder. 2. Verify that the static meshes are correctly imported. ## Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018466585) 1. Locate your MetaHuman in the **Content Browser**. * Or, run it through the right-click Context Menu → MetaHuman → MetaHuman Character to create a new MetaHuman 2. **Double-click** the MetaHuman to open the **MetaHuman Editor**. 3. Export the MetaHuman as a **Combined Skeletal Mesh** : * MetaHuman Editor Main Menu → MetaHuman Creator → Export Combined Skel Mesh * Save this mesh inside the **Skeletal Meshes** folder of your USD asset directory. ## Step 3. Create Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799079787033) 1. In the **Static Meshes** folder: * **Right-click** → **Physics > Cloth Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., CA_name). 2. **Open Cloth Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Right-click the Cloth Asset → **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. 3. **Clean up nodes** : * Delete everything except: * USD Import * Transfer Skin Weights * Remesh * Remesh LOD2 (optional for extra LOD) * Cloth Asset Terminal. ## Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799641793433) 1. **Add Static Mesh Import Node** : * Right-click background → **Create Node: Static Mesh Import**. * Assign your USD static mesh to this node. 2. **Connect Nodes** : * Static Mesh Import → Transfer Skin Weights. * Transfer Skin Weights → Cloth Asset Terminal. * Also connect: * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh → Collection LOD0. * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh LOD2 → Cloth Asset Terminal (optional). 3. **Configure Transfer Skin Weights Node** : * Target Meshes: **Render Mesh**. * Render Mesh Transfer: **Skeletal Mesh**. * Transform Method: **Closest Point on Surface**. * Assign the **Combined Skeletal Mesh** to the Skeletal Mesh property. 4. **Preview** : * Switch the left window view to **Render** for visualization. ## Step 5. Organize Assets ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881262873) 1. Create a new folder inside the Basic**Mesh** folder. 2. Move: * Static Mesh * Cloth Asset * Cloth Asset Node into this folder. ## Step 6. Create Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881264409) 1. In **Static Mesh Folder** : * **Right-click** → **Physics > Outfit Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., OA_name). 2. Select **Resizable Outfit Template** when prompted. 3. Move the Outfit Asset node into the folder created earlier. ## Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581027609) 1. **Open Outfit Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Double-click the Outfit Asset. 2. Change **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** from **Automatic** to **Manual**. 3. **Add Source Asset** : * Select **Sized Outfit Source** → Click **+**. * Drag the Cloth Asset into the Source Asset option. * Assign a size name. 4. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** and wait for completion. 5. Open **Source Body Slider** : * Drag and drop the Combined Skeletal Mesh. 6. Enable **Sized Outfit** checkbox to make it resizable. 7. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** again, then switch back to **Automatic**. ## Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581029657) 1. Open MetaHuman Editor. 2. Go to the **Hair and Clothing** tab. 3. Drag and drop the **Outfit Asset** from the Content Drawer into the Outfit Clothing section. 4. In the Body tab, change the model's size parameters to adjust MetaHuman proportions, and confirm that the outfit adapts dynamically. 5. **Verify** that the outfit adjusts automatically to match the Metahuman's new size. ## ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility The use of ChaosCloth assets from USD data exported from Marvelous Designer is subject to the following compatibility restrictions based on the Unreal Engine version: * **Marvelous Designer 2025.0:** Compatible only with **UE 5.4**. * **Marvelous Designer 2025.2:** Compatible with **UE 5.6** and later version. * **UE 5.5:** Not compatible due to technical issues regarding simulation data. ※ Note: This issue is specific to **ChaosCloth**. Regular meshes and materials are unaffected.
content_description: This guide provides a step-by-step workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD files and integrating them seamlessly with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman character system.

title: OBJ Trim Properties
content: ### Objective When an OBJ is imported as a Garment, input weight and reflect it in the Simulation. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern [ Z ] / Transform Pattern [ A ] 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern ### Operation 1. Select the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Select the loaded OBJ trim. →The OBJ properties are displayed in Property Editor. 3. Modify the properties according to the following. Information | Name | Enter a name and an item number of the trim. ---|---|--- Specification | Scale | Scale trim with X, Y, and Z-axis. Weight | Set the weight of trim. The entered value of weight is reflected in the simulation. Collision (Ver. 11) | Set whether you turn the Collision on or off. It only enables or disables the Collision of detached trim. Collision Thickness | Set the Collision Thickness with a garment. The higher the value is, the farther the distance with a garment is in the simulation. Material | Set the Material of trim. Polygon Optimization (ver. 2024.1) | Count | Set the number of polygons. ---|---|--- Plane | This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for importing and modifying OBJ garments, allowing users to input weight for accurate simulation and adjust various properties through the Property Editor.
